claims.statement: > **Quick answer:** Looking for a **gobymeds discount code**? GobyMeds’ promotion page lists STARTNOW25 for specified starter compounded bundles, while two percentage-off campaigns have stated 2025 end dates. Treat these as reported terms, not checkout-tested savings. Confirm the exact product, restrictions and final total with GobyMeds before paying; clinical eligibility remains a separate decision.

The provider’s promotion page displays a last-revision date of May 25, 2026. Its Starter Bundle Sales Disclaimer lists **STARTNOW25** for $25 off the specified three-month starter compounded bundles. It lists a compounded semaglutide starter bundle at $299, or $274 with the discount, and a compounded tirzepatide starter bundle at $399, or $374 with the discount. These are provider-reported bundle amounts, not an independently verified complete bill or confirmed checkout acceptance.

That same section says the coupon is limited to one per customer, cannot be used with other offers, applies only to the listed products and is available while supplies last. GobyMeds reserves the right to modify or terminate the promotion without notice. There is no assurance in this guide that those conditions have been satisfied for your account or that the offer remains redeemable.

The Jump Start section lists **JUMPSTART20** for 20% off, with exclusions, a three-use limit and no combination with other offers. It also states that the offer ended December 31, 2025 at 11:59 PM EST and excludes Zepbound and Wegovy. The date has passed as of our October 9, 2026 source check. A more recent revision date at the top of the page does not, by itself, extend that stated campaign deadline.

The Black Friday section similarly lists **BLACKFRIDAY20**, but gives an end date of December 7, 2025 at 11:59 PM EST. Its listed restrictions include one coupon per customer, no combination with other offers, supplies availability and exclusions for Zepbound and Wegovy. We do not present either of these percentage-off codes as a currently working offer.

A separate GobyMeds PCOS-awareness page describes **GOBYPCOS** and a $25 discount during September, with first-month wording in its order instructions. We checked the page in October. The captured campaign text does not establish a currently available October offer or a newly extended campaign. We do not adopt its medical marketing as independent clinical evidence.

The source’s STARTNOW25 wording applies to its specified starter compounded bundles. It does not say that every medication, every plan duration, every repeat purchase or every customer qualifies. The captured description is narrower than a general “$25 off GobyMeds” headline.

The provider’s starter-bundle section contains multiple conditions: one coupon per customer, no other offers, listed products only, supplies availability and a right to modify or terminate. A reader who sees only “$25 off” has not yet checked the complete source description.

The current page contains both a 2026 revision heading and campaign sections with 2025 end dates. Those are different pieces of evidence. The revision heading shows what the page reports about its own update; it does not erase a deadline inside an individual offer.

The public starter-bundle figures are useful only within their stated scope. They are not a verified renewal price, a complete list of possible charges or proof of a recurring discount. We have not established what additional fees, changes or exclusions apply to a specific proposed order.

GobyMeds’ promotion disclaimer says medications are prescribed by licensed healthcare professionals only after an online consultation to determine eligibility. That is a provider-reported statement; we have not independently verified an individual clinician’s license, the service process or a particular reader’s eligibility. A discount description does not supply that verification.

FDA advises patients considering these drugs to obtain a prescription from their doctor and fill it at a state-licensed pharmacy. FDA also says compounded drugs should be used only when a patient’s medical needs cannot be met by an FDA-approved drug. Those are general U.S. recommendations, not a conclusion about this provider or an individual proposed prescription.

FDA’s unapproved-GLP-1 information says unapproved versions do not undergo FDA review for safety, effectiveness and quality before they are marketed. Its patient recommendations distinguish compounded use from an FDA-approved drug that can meet a patient’s medical needs. A promotional reduction does not resolve that distinction.

The FDA-hosted Wegovy prescribing-information PDF identifies semaglutide injection and tablets on original physical page 1 and includes product-specific contraindications and warnings. The approved product’s label is not approval of a compounded preparation or certification of a telehealth company. We do not use its existence to endorse a provider’s products or a coupon.

A retrospective study of 15,811 commercially insured U.S. adults starting branded semaglutide associated discontinuation with copayment amount and other characteristics. This observational evidence is not a study of GobyMeds customers or proof that a coupon prevents discontinuation. It supports asking about later costs, not treating a smaller introductory payment as a long-term affordability answer. [S7]

In a selected sample of 288 adults who discontinued injectable semaglutide or tirzepatide within their first treatment year, cost or insurance issues were the most commonly recorded reason. The study used one health system in Ohio and Florida and excluded type 2 diabetes. Its selected sample does not establish the proportion of all patients who discontinue or a discount’s effect on outcomes. [S8]

An economic commentary notes financing challenges, coverage restrictions and mixed evidence on medical-spending impact for branded weight-loss medications. It does not substantiate a provider-specific financial return or the cost-effectiveness of a compounded product. Compare the introductory order with the next order’s independently stated cost; do not count promised future healthcare savings as money available to pay either bill. [S9]

sections.heading: Seven checks before you rely on a code
paragraphs: 1. Match the merchant, not just the word “Goby”.

Start with the exact website and provider name. This article concerns GobyMeds and its own captured promotion pages. A similarly named business or a search result containing “Goby” is not automatically the same merchant. We do not use discounts for a different business to fill an apparent gap in GobyMeds evidence.

Do not infer current acceptance from a coupon directory’s “verified” badge, a user comment or a social post. Those are separate sources with their own verification methods and dates. Our conclusions above rest on provider-reported terms, and even those terms are not a substitute for a current order-specific confirmation.
2. Identify the exact qualifying product and plan.

The source’s STARTNOW25 wording applies to its specified starter compounded bundles. It does not say that every medication, every plan duration, every repeat purchase or every customer qualifies. The captured description is narrower than a general “$25 off GobyMeds” headline. [S2]

Ask for the plan name as it appears on the order, its stated duration, what is included and the amount due. Keep the provider’s description separate from a clinician’s treatment decision. This guide does not recommend choosing a compounded drug, a brand, a quantity or a treatment duration to make a discount fit.

If a proposed order is changed after clinical review, recheck the commercial terms for the revised order. Do not assume a code for the original description transfers automatically. The practical goal is a clear bill for whatever care is appropriately prescribed, not a treatment choice driven by a coupon.
3. Read the restriction, not only the headline amount.

The provider’s starter-bundle section contains multiple conditions: one coupon per customer, no other offers, listed products only, supplies availability and a right to modify or terminate. A reader who sees only “$25 off” has not yet checked the complete source description. [S2]

Ask whether your account has already used the relevant offer and whether a different promotion is being considered. We do not establish how the provider applies those terms to a particular customer. An untested interpretation such as “use a second code later” should not be presented as a verified way around a restriction.
4. Verify the date on the specific campaign.

The current page contains both a 2026 revision heading and campaign sections with 2025 end dates. Those are different pieces of evidence. The revision heading shows what the page reports about its own update; it does not erase a deadline inside an individual offer. [S2]

For a code with no visible end date in the captured section, do not invent a deadline or assume it runs indefinitely. Ask whether the stated offer is currently available for the exact order. A later source check may find different terms, but future checks have not already happened.
5. Compare the full amount due, not a promotional fraction.

The public starter-bundle figures are useful only within their stated scope. They are not a verified renewal price, a complete list of possible charges or proof of a recurring discount. We have not established what additional fees, changes or exclusions apply to a specific proposed order. [S2]

Ask the provider to identify the amount due before payment and what it covers. Questions worth clarifying include the stated plan duration, any separately billed service, shipping, additional items and the terms for a later purchase. These are questions, not a claim that any particular additional charge is imposed.

Avoid turning a bundle total into a guaranteed monthly rate. A plan described in weeks, a calendar-month statement and a recurring billing arrangement are different descriptions. Without a precise written explanation for the proposed order, simple division can create a misleading comparison.

For broader fee questions, see our [online GLP-1 provider fee comparison guide](/guides/compare-online-glp-1-provider-fees/). It does not establish that a GobyMeds coupon applies to your order, and this coupon guide does not independently validate every broader provider term.
6. Keep checkout acceptance and medical eligibility separate.

GobyMeds’ promotion disclaimer says medications are prescribed by licensed healthcare professionals only after an online consultation to determine eligibility. That is a provider-reported statement; we have not independently verified an individual clinician’s license, the service process or a particular reader’s eligibility. A discount description does not supply that verification. [S2]

FDA advises patients considering these drugs to obtain a prescription from their doctor and fill it at a state-licensed pharmacy. FDA also says compounded drugs should be used only when a patient’s medical needs cannot be met by an FDA-approved drug. Those are general U.S. recommendations, not a conclusion about this provider or an individual proposed prescription. [S4]

If you need an answer about treatment suitability, follow up with the treating clinician rather than attempting to decide it from a promotional page. We do not calculate eligibility, suggest a dose or describe a discount as evidence that a medicine is safe or appropriate for you.
7. Understand what would happen after an order change.

Before relying on a quoted saving, ask what happens if the proposed order changes, the clinical consultation does not lead to the originally expected prescription or the promotion is no longer available. We have not established the provider’s answer for a particular situation.

Ask separately about the applicable cancellation, refund and subsequent-purchase terms. A coupon article should not silently turn unanswered questions into promises of a refund, automatic renewal discount or guaranteed supply. The absence of an answer in our evidence is a limitation, not a finding that the provider has a favorable or unfavorable policy.
